jobs.description:
The YMCA of Moore County offers an opportunity for a community-focused leader to guide a strong, stable organization with deep local roots.

Job Description

YMCA OF MOORE COUNTY

POSITION:
Chief Executive Officer

Application Deadline:
August 13, 2026

Address

1400 S. Maddox

Dumas, Texas 79029

Web Address: https://www.moorecountyymca.com

The YMCA of Moore County is an equal opportunity employer. We work to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to reach their full potential with dignity.

THE OPPORTUNITY AT THE YMCA OF MOORE COUNTY

The YMCA of Moore County offers an opportunity for a community-focused leader to guide a strong, stable organization with deep local roots. With more than $1.3 million invested in recent facility improvements and a debt-free, financially sound operation, the YMCA is well positioned for continued success.

This is an opportunity to build on momentum. The CEO will serve as the visible leader of the organization, strengthening relationships with members, staff, and community partners while ensuring programs reflect local needs.

With opportunities to expand programming and deepen engagement, the next CEO will be able to make a direct and meaningful impact. Supported by an engaged Board and committed staff team, the CEO will help ensure the YMCA remains a vital resource for individuals and families across Moore County.

Qualifications

Criteria for Candidates:

Accredited four-year college degree and/or equivalent work experience.
Fiscally sound business management approach with a proven record of budgetary and fiscal leadership for an organization of more than $1.4 million annually.
Minimum of seven years of senior management experience with a YMCA or comparable organization, including direct supervision of multiple levels of staff and employees.
Demonstrated ability to develop and strengthen community relationships.
Ability to develop innovative programs and evaluate existing or proposed programs for financial effectiveness, community relevance, and broader engagement.
Strategic planning and fundraising experience, including annual campaigns and grant opportunities.
Current YMCA Organizational Leader Certification or ability to obtain certification within three years.

Essential Functions

KEY SKILLS AND ABILITIES OF OUR NEXT CEO

Skills

The board believes its next CEO should be an experienced, community-minded leader with the skills and background needed to achieve excellence in the following areas:

Develop and Implement a Strategic Plan:
Work effectively with volunteers, community leaders, and key staff to create and implement a strategic plan that addresses the needs of the communities served by the Y. The plan should include clear organizational strategies, defined deliverables, and measurable goals. Key Competencies: Change Leadership, Communication & Influence, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Program/Project Management

Fiscal Management:
Use high-level financial analysis to forecast trends, support growth, and maintain financial stability. Lead the organization toward balanced or surplus operations by growing earned revenue and contributions, controlling expenses, and guiding staff leaders toward strong departmental performance. Develop and implement stewardship strategies that strengthen long-term sustainability. Key Competencies: Fiscal Management, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Developing Self & Others, Philanthropy

Improve Operating Performance:
Engage the board and appropriate staff in developing an annual tactical plan that identifies key goals and objectives and supports safe, relevant, and sustainable operations. Key Competencies: Developing Self & Others, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Innovation

Position the Y as a Vital Partner for Community Change:
Serve as an ambassador for the mission, purpose, and vision for the YMCA within the community and cultivate strong relationships with key stakeholders. Key Competencies: Communication & Influence, Engaging Community, Collaboration

Build and Lead Staff:
Ensure a talent development system is in place and executed effectively while fostering a collaborative, mission-driven culture. Key Competencies: Developing Self & Others, Inclusion, Emotional Maturity, Change Leadership

Steward Fundraising Efforts:
Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan that strengthens the YMCA’s impact through donor engagement and community support. Key Competencies: Philanthropy, Engaging Community, Communication & Influence

About The Ymca Of Moore County

The YMCA of Moore County has served the Dumas community and surrounding area since 1960. Today, it supports more than 3,000 members and operates with an annual budget of approximately $1.4 million. The organization is financially stable and debt-free, reflecting a long-standing commitment to responsible stewardship and sustainability.

Governed by a dedicated and engaged Board of Directors, the YMCA is supported by a committed staff team and a strong culture of collaboration and service. Together, they have established the YMCA as a trusted and valued presence in the community.

In recent years, the YMCA has invested significantly in its facilities, including upgrades to wellness areas, locker rooms, and program spaces, ensuring a quality experience for members and participants.

Located adjacent to the city’s main park and across from a new elementary school, the YMCA is a convenient and welcoming place for youth, families, and individuals to participate in programs that support health, wellness, and connection.

Our Mission

To put Christian principles into practice through programs that build a healthy spirit, mind, and body for all.

Our Cause & Values

To strengthen the foundations of community and instill the values of caring, honesty, respect, and responsibility.

Our Culture

The Y Experience –
The Y Experience is built from our mission and encompasses the values and philosophy by which we serve and operate

Welcoming –
We are open to all. We are a place where you can be yourself and find yourself in others.

Genuine –
We value you and embrace your individuality.

Hopeful –
We believe in you and your potential to do good in the world.

Nurturing –
We support you as you become the best-version-of-yourself.

Determined –
Above all else, we are on a relentless quest to make our community stronger, beginning with you

About Our Community

Dumas, Texas, is a welcoming Panhandle city located about 45 miles north of Amarillo. Known for its strong civic pride and neighborly spirit, Dumas offers a family-oriented quality of life with affordable living, short commute times, open spaces, and access to regional resources.

Residents benefit from local schools, healthcare services, parks, youth sports, a public library, and a college campus, along with community events that bring people together throughout the year. The area supports an active and engaged population with a strong sense of connection.

The local economy includes agriculture, manufacturing, energy, transportation, and small businesses, providing a stable foundation for the community and the surrounding region.

Benefits

The YMCA of Moore County offers a competitive benefits package that includes participation in the YMCA Retirement Plan, a 403(b) savings plan, health insurance, paid time off, and additional benefits in accordance with YMCA personnel policies.

Residency Expectation:
Living in the YMCA’s service area is required.

Criteria For Candidates

Accredited four-year college degree and/or equivalent work experience.
Fiscally sound business management approach with a proven record of budgetary and fiscal leadership for an organization of more than $1.4 million annually.
Minimum of seven years of senior management experience with a YMCA or comparable organization, including direct supervision of multiple levels of staff and employees.
Demonstrated ability to develop and strengthen community relationships.
Ability to develop innovative programs and evaluate existing or proposed programs for financial effectiveness, community relevance, and broader engagement.
Strategic planning and fundraising experience, including annual campaigns and grant opportunities.
Current YMCA Organizational Leader Certification or ability to obtain certification within three years.

SEARCH PROCESS TARGET DATES

Applications accepted through: August 13, 2026
Preliminary interviews scheduled: Week of September 21
In-person interviews: October 20 and October 21, 2026
CEO selection made: Week of October 26, 2026
New CEO on board: Targeted for December 1, 2026, or as mutually agreed upon
dates subject to change

How To Apply

References, Background Check, and Organizational Leader Certification:

Candidates must submit a resume and cover letter in PDF format as part of the online application. Applications submitted without a cover letter will not be considered.

Candidates who advance to final interviews will be asked to submit six references, including four professional and two personal references. References will be checked only with prior notification. The successful candidate must pass a background check and have a current Y-USA Organizational Leader Certification or obtain certification within the first three years as CEO. The YMCA’s personnel policies may require additional screening.

https://tinyurl.com/Y-of-Moore-County-CEO

Why You'll Love Working Here

Lead a beautifully remodeled senior living community with strong occupancy and a supportive regional leadership team behind you. At Americare Senior Living, you'll enjoy competitive pay with bonus potential, meaningful career growth, and a servant-hearted culture where you can make a lasting impact on residents and team members every day.

We’ve been consistently certified as a Great Place to Work, ranked on Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Aging Services, and named one of the 2025 Best Senior Living providers by U.S. News & World Report.

Your Role as the Executive Director / Administrator

Americare Senior Living is seeking a dedicated Executive Director / Administrator
to lead the day-to-day operations of our Assisted Living / Residential Living Community
. In this highly visible leadership role, you’ll be responsible for fostering a warm, nurturing environment that enhances the quality of life for both residents and team members.

As the Executive Director / Administrator, you’ll oversee all aspects of community operations, ensuring compliance with state and federal regulations while driving excellence in care, culture, and performance.

This Role May Also Be Known As

Executive Director, Assisted Living Administrator, Community Administrator, Senior Living Administrator, or Residential Living Administrator, Residential Care Facility Administrator, Continuing Care Rewtirement Community Administrator,

What You’ll Do

Leadership & Community Management

Lead with a resident-first mindset, prioritizing compassionate care, safety, and quality of life.
Set clear expectations, model accountability, and foster a positive, service-oriented culture.

Team Collaboration & Development

Cultivate a culture of teamwork, transparency, and open communication across all departments.
Hire, train, coach, and develop a high-performing team of caregivers and support staff.

Operational Excellence

Oversee medical, nursing, and administrative functions to ensure smooth and effective daily operations.
Enforce policies and procedures that support high standards of care and regulatory compliance.

Fiscal & Performance Management

Develop and manage the community budget, monitor expenses, revenue, and occupancy.
Identify opportunities for cost efficiencies, revenue growth, and operational improvement.

Community & Family Engagement

Build strong, trusting relationships with residents and their families.
Engage with the local community to promote Americare’s mission and strengthen the community’s reputation.

Facility & Asset Management

Oversee building maintenance, improvements, and equipment upgrades to ensure a safe, welcoming environment for residents and team members.

What You Bring

Licensure & Credentials

Current state Administrator licensure or certification, as required by state regulations.
Certified Medication Aide (CMA) or Certified Medication Technician (CMT), if required by the state.
Valid driver’s license with a good driving record.

Education

Bachelor’s degree preferred. Relevant fields may include Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Nursing, Gerontology, or a related discipline.

Experience

Must be at least 18 years of age.
Proven experience successfully managing, leading, and developing teams in a senior living or healthcare leadership role.

Skills & Knowledge

Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to build trust and relationships with residents, families, team members, and community partners.
Solid understanding of healthcare regulations, medical terminology, medication management protocols, and compliance standards.

Physical Demands

Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 50 pounds.
Occasionally assist with safely transferring residents.
Vision requirements include near and far vision with good depth perception.

Join Americare Senior Living
and lead with compassion while driving the success of an Assisted Living Community that truly makes a difference. Take the next step in your leadership career and help shape a place residents are proud to call home.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Americare Senior Living is committed to equal employment opportunities and welcomes applicants from all walks of life. We value diversity and strive to create a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging.

jobs.title: Executive Director of Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Job Title
Executive Director of Technology Operations

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment

Partner with product management, engineering, IT, finance, HR, and business leaders to align technology operations with business priorities.
Facilitate communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support enterprise transformation initiatives and technology-enabled business growth.
Ensure effective coordination across global technology teams.

VIII. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead high-performing technology operations teams.
Develop leadership capabilities, succession planning, and talent development programs.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
Promote employee engagement and collaboration across technology functions.

Qualifications
Education Background

Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related fields.
Master’s degree or MBA preferred.

THE OPPORTUNITY AT THE YMCA OF MOORE COUNTY

The YMCA of Moore County offers an opportunity for a community-focused leader to guide a strong, stable organization with deep local roots. With more than $1.3 million invested in recent facility improvements and a debt-free, financially sound operation, the YMCA is well positioned for continued success.

This is an opportunity to build on momentum. The CEO will serve as the visible leader of the organization, strengthening relationships with members, staff, and community partners while ensuring programs reflect local needs.

With opportunities to expand programming and deepen engagement, the next CEO will be able to make a direct and meaningful impact. Supported by an engaged Board and committed staff team, the CEO will help ensure the YMCA remains a vital resource for individuals and families across Moore County.

Accredited four-year college degree and/or equivalent work experience.
Fiscally sound business management approach with a proven record of budgetary and fiscal leadership for an organization of more than $1.4 million annually.
Minimum of seven years of senior management experience with a YMCA or comparable organization, including direct supervision of multiple levels of staff and employees.
Demonstrated ability to develop and strengthen community relationships.
Ability to develop innovative programs and evaluate existing or proposed programs for financial effectiveness, community relevance, and broader engagement.
Strategic planning and fundraising experience, including annual campaigns and grant opportunities.

KEY SKILLS AND ABILITIES OF OUR NEXT CEO

Skills

Develop and implement stewardship strategies that strengthen long-term sustainability. Key Competencies: Fiscal Management, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Developing Self & Others, Philanthropy

Improve Operating Performance:

Build and Lead Staff:
Ensure a talent development system is in place and executed effectively while fostering a collaborative, mission-driven culture. Key Competencies: Developing Self & Others, Inclusion, Emotional Maturity, Change Leadership

Steward Fundraising Efforts:
Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan that strengthens the YMCA’s impact through donor engagement and community support. Key Competencies: Philanthropy, Engaging Community, Communication & Influence

About The Ymca Of Moore County

The YMCA of Moore County has served the Dumas community and surrounding area since 1960. Today, it supports more than 3,000 members and operates with an annual budget of approximately $1.4 million. The organization is financially stable and debt-free, reflecting a long-standing commitment to responsible stewardship and sustainability.

Governed by a dedicated and engaged Board of Directors, the YMCA is supported by a committed staff team and a strong culture of collaboration and service. Together, they have established the YMCA as a trusted and valued presence in the community.

In recent years, the YMCA has invested significantly in its facilities, including upgrades to wellness areas, locker rooms, and program spaces, ensuring a quality experience for members and participants.

Located adjacent to the city’s main park and across from a new elementary school, the YMCA is a convenient and welcoming place for youth, families, and individuals to participate in programs that support health, wellness, and connection.

Dumas, Texas, is a welcoming Panhandle city located about 45 miles north of Amarillo. Known for its strong civic pride and neighborly spirit, Dumas offers a family-oriented quality of life with affordable living, short commute times, open spaces, and access to regional resources.

Job Title

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Director of Technology Operations is responsible for leading the operational management, governance, and execution of the company’s technology organization. This role ensures that technology resources, systems, infrastructure, development processes, and operational activities are aligned with business objectives and delivered efficiently, securely, and at scale.

The Executive Director of Technology Operations serves as the critical bridge between technology strategy and operational execution, driving operational excellence, technology governance, digital transformation, and cross-functional collaboration to support sustainable business growth and innovation.

Key Responsibilities
I. Technology Operations Strategy and Execution

Develop and implement technology operations strategies aligned with corporate and technology objectives.
Translate technology roadmaps into operational plans and measurable outcomes.
Drive operational excellence across software development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud operations, and IT service delivery.
Establish governance frameworks to ensure efficient execution of technology initiatives.

II. Technology Program and Portfolio Management

Oversee the planning, execution, and delivery of enterprise technology projects and programs.
Manage technology portfolios, budgets, resources, and priorities to maximize business value.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
Develop executive dashboards and reporting mechanisms to provide visibility into technology performance.

III. Technology Process Optimization and Governance

Establish and standardize technology operational processes, policies, and procedures.
Implement best practices across software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps, ITSM, Agile, and project management disciplines.
Continuously improve operational efficiency through process automation and workflow optimization.
Ensure compliance with internal controls, governance standards, and regulatory requirements.

IV. Infrastructure, Cloud, and Service Operations

Oversee enterprise technology infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, and operational support services.
Ensure system availability, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Drive service delivery excellence through effective monitoring, incident management, and problem resolution.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience initiatives.

V. Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Compliance

Collaborate with cybersecurity teams to ensure protection of enterprise systems, applications, and data assets.
Identify and mitigate technology-related operational risks.
Ensure compliance with industry regulations, security frameworks, and corporate governance requirements.
Establish risk management and escalation procedures for critical technology operations.

VI. Data, Analytics, and Performance Management

Define and monitor technology KPIs, SLAs, and operational performance metrics.
Utilize data analytics to improve operational efficiency and support decision-making.
Develop performance reporting frameworks for executive leadership.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives based on operational insights and business needs.

VII. Cross-functional Collaboration and Business Alignment
